result:
Fair enough. You've told me what you want; how to build it is mine to call, so here's the one choice that shapes the write-up, briefly:

**1. Add it to the existing taproom app (my pick).** New tables in the same SQLite database for batches, sack lots, what went into each batch, and bottling runs, plus a few new pages. Brewers use a cheap barcode scanner that types into a tablet page, so wet hands never touch a keyboard. The bottling page sends the batch number and date to the label printer. One app, one database, one backup, on the Pi you already run.

**2. A separate small app on the same Pi.** Keeps brewing data fully apart from the bar tabs. A bug in one can't touch the other. The cost is two apps to start, update and back up, and twelve years of records split across two places for no gain you've asked for.

I dropped off-the-shelf brewery software. You'd be fitting your process to theirs, and it wouldn't print your labels the way you described.

I'm going with option 1.

This is big enough to need a proper written design: new tables, scanner input, and printer output. I'll write it to `specs/batch-tracking.md` next. Before you see it, a reviewer will read it as if they had to build from it. I may come back once with a few questions only you can answer, then hand it to you for approval. Say so if you'd rather I went with option 2.
